newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end pit trading barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end pit trading barely mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended barely mixed after a session of cautious pit trading.

Traders said one fund bought some 1,500 March yen futures toward the close but other units stayed quiet as Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan continued his question-and-answer session to a House committee Wednesday.

Shortly after futures shut, Greenspan said the U.S. economy is doing "exceptionally well" from the Fed's viewpoint and that he is skeptical of arguments saying faster growth alone leads to inflation. He also said monetary policy is not a tool to prick the stock market bubble.

Greenspan's remarks dovetailed with sentiment that the U.S. economy is stronger than many G7 economies including Germany, Switzerland and Japan, an argument bearish brokers trotted out to bolster their forecasts for more downside soon in most currencies.
"The dollar is in a one-way trend," said one floor broker. "This place (futures) is going one way, and that is down."
Others also said technicals still favored lower futures prices, especially in marks after the last couple weak closes.
But uncertainty about U.S. and German jobs data this week afternoon kept most units range-bound on light turnover.
Near the close, marks nosed back down toward the morning's low, just above March contract low at $0.5830 hit overnight after German industrial output fell more than expected.
Although the drop in construction was linked partly to poor weather, it still served to highlight the soft state of the German economy, brokers said.
At the same time, EMU-delay rumors and denials sent many mark players to the sidelines.
"Each time, it moved us 10 ticks either way," another floor broker said of the EMU rumors. "If they delay, it's good for the mark."
A German spokesman Wednesday denied rumors that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was seeking a delay in the 1999 EMU startup or that he was about to resign over the issue.
Yen gained on crosses and also after Japan's trade surplus surged 53.3 percent during the first 20 days of February.

Subtle hints that Japanese rates could head upward added yen support. Japan's chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama said Japan should consider measures to deal with the impact low interest rates have on people's incomes.
Mexican peso futures cut their biggest losses, with a third broker saying that unit looked oversold.
He also noted that March peso futures broke below a double bottom at $0.123000 but settled Wednesday above there.

March yen rose $0.000060 to $0.008260, marks rose $0.0006 to $0.5843, Swiss francs gained $0.0024 to $0.6757, sterling ended flat at $1.6128, Canadian dollar rose $0.0006 to $0.7311, Aussie dollar lost $0.0046 to $0.7847, and Mexican peso fell $0.000400 to $0.123900.
